newsitem.title: INDIA: Suzuki's India venture will need equity. [CORRECTED 09:57 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Suzuki's India venture will need equity. [CORRECTED 09:57 GMT]

text.p: Maruti Udyog Ltd managing director R.C. Bhargava said on Monday that the Indo-Japanese car maker would need to raise fresh equity to increase capacity and fend off competition.

"At a suitable point in time we will need to raise equity," Bhargava told reporters after a seminar on Indo-Japanese relations in the Indian capital. He declined to say how much equity would be needed or when.
Bhargava declined to comment on remarks last Friday by Industry Minister Murasoli Maran, who said the Indian government had decided not to allow a change in the equity structure of Maruti Udyog.
"The equity structure between the two partners is really a matter between the partners," Bhargava said. "Management really should not have a view to express on that issue."
Currently Japan's Suzuki Motor Co and the Indian government each hold 50 percent stakes in Maruti Udyog, which controls 70 percent of India's car market.
Maruti faces the prospect of stiff competition.
Among firms to have entered India since 1991 are South General Motors Co of the United States, France's Peugeot SA and Japan's Honda Motor Co Ltd and Toyota Motor Corp.
Analysts have said that Suzuki would like to increase its stake in the 15-year-old joint venture.
Bhargava said the Indian government had not been willing in the past to match increases in Suzuki's equity stake, which he said stood at 26 percent until 1988 and 40 percent until 1992.
"But I cannot speak (about) what they will decide in the future. It is a decision which will vary, I guess, on the government's thinking from time to time," Bhargava said.

Bhargava told the seminar that over the past two years at Maruti, there had been "a blurring of roles, some lost confidence and trust" which he said possibly reflected changes in personnel. He did not elaborate.
The carmaker's managing director told reporters later that at some indefinite point in the future, Maruti would have to increase its equity base.

"We will certainly have to expand our investment volumes in the coming years. Money will be required for new models, expansion of capacity will be required, better productivity will be required for better quality," he said.
"I would imagine that if not today, in the future certainly there will be the need to raise equity because Maruti can raise equity at a premium, whereas loans in India are very expensive," he said.

"I'm not saying that we have to raise equity today. But we will in the future certainly need to raise equity, and this question will have to be answered, if not today, maybe six months later, a year later, sometime it has to be addressed."
Bhargava said Suzuki generally advocated increasing investment resources through a mixture of equity, loans and internal resources.

"If we have to invest in the next five years something close to, let's say, 70 billion rupees ($1.95 billion), according to Suzuki's experience, about one third should be in equity, that means you'll need to raise something like 23 billion to 25 billion as equity," he said.

Bhargava said an increase in equity of that magnitude would raise the face value of Maruti's equity base to about 1.92 billion rupees from the current 1.32 billion. (Corrects to make clear equity based has changed to 1.92 billion rupees, not 19.2 billion rupees, and has changed from 1.32 billion and not 13.2 billion as originally stated.)
"Don't take this as any approved investment," he said. "So on that basis, that is the kind of money that has to come in as equity...This is totally hypothetical."
-- New Delhi newsroom +91-11 301 2024 ($1 = 35.9 rupees)
